source_read: Publisher full text (HTML), https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/74/wr/mm7432a1.htm, read in the app's browser in a tab of my own: Summary box, abstract, every section, all main-text footnotes, the Figure 1 and Figure 2 captions and footnotes, and the Table with all its footnotes (rendered as text). Every with- and without-opioid pair in all 36 Table rows was summed for the three stimulant groups, and the age, sex and race columns were checked against the column totals. The two misprinted cells were confirmed in the page's table cells. Figures 1 and 2 are images (values not extracted beyond the text); the Supplementary Figure and the PDF were not opened.

key_findings.correction: Write the involvement rule as the footnote gives it: a drug counts as involved if the medical examiner or coroner listed it as a cause of death on the death certificate, in the medical examiner or coroner report or in the postmortem toxicology report (main-text footnote §§; also Table footnote * and Figure 1 footnote §§). The finding says 'as listed by the medical examiner or coroner', which drops 'as a cause of death' and reads like detection. Everything else is confirmed: Data Sources 1st and 2nd paragraphs, Statistical Analysis 1st and 2nd paragraphs, footnote † (ICD-10 codes plus text searches of literal cause-of-death fields) and ¶¶ (2000 US standard population).

key_findings.note: Main-text footnotes †††, §§§ (46 states and DC; I counted the list: California, Idaho, North Dakota and Texas are the absent states) and ¶¶¶ (32 jurisdictions for the full period, 15 for at least one 6-month period; 93.1%); Table circumstance row N = 226,698. Two precision points. (1) The printed rule is that a jurisdiction had to report at least 75% of its deaths in at least one 6-month period. 'Included for 6-month periods in which they reported at least 75%' is an inference, supported by 'California and Wisconsin were included for a subset of the time frame'. (2) The bare symbols are ambiguous next to the Table, which reuses †††, §§§ and ¶¶¶ for other content (history of stimulant use, history of opioid use, the treatment definition). 'Main-text footnotes' would remove the ambiguity.
Table Overall row and Results > SUDORS 2nd paragraph; all six percentages recomputed from the counts.

Table age and sex rows; Results > SUDORS 2nd paragraph (66.5% vs 44.2%, which the age rows reproduce: 25.7 + 29.6 + 11.2 and 22.0 + 17.8 + 4.4). The editors' 64% vs 39% reproduces (19,350/30,124 and 25,770/66,463).

Table circumstance rows, methamphetamine columns, and Table footnote *** (hypertension excluded); Results > SUDORS 3rd paragraph (38.7% vs 21.2% for any stimulant, and 'comparable' patterns for methamphetamine and cocaine).
Results > NVSS 1st paragraph and abstract; no figures for the opioid-stratified trends in the text.
Introduction 1st paragraph, citing NCHS Data Brief 522 (their ref. 1); main-text footnote * for the provisional 2024 data.
Discussion > Limitations (one paragraph). The third limitation also says the circumstance percentages are likely underestimated.

key_findings.correction: Replace 'the 38.7% cardiovascular history of stimulant-only decedents' with 'the 38.7% cardiovascular history of decedents with stimulants and no opioids'. In this report 'only stimulants' is a different, narrower category (14.5% of deaths, no other drug contributing; Figure 1 footnote **). The 38.7% belongs to the 'stimulants and no opioids' group (49,209 deaths; circumstance subset 34,575), which can include other non-opioid drugs. The rest is confirmed: Discussion 2nd paragraph (about 10% of all US adults), 4th (drug-checking inference) and 5th (possibly long-term stimulant use).

reporting_issues.note: The page's table cell reads '2,236 (73.8)'. 30,139 - 7,903 = 22,236, and 47,503 + 22,236 = 69,739, the methamphetamine male total. In my full pass this is the only cell that breaks a with-plus-without sum in the methamphetamine columns.

Cell '2,819 (1.6)'; 1,820 + 1,071 = 2,891. Every other with-plus-without pair in all 36 rows sums exactly for any stimulant, cocaine and methamphetamine. Both values round to 1.6% of the column, so the percentage cannot decide which cell is wrong.

Results > SUDORS 1st paragraph; Figure 1 caption 'N = 309,274'. Read as a share of all deaths, 14.5% fits beside the 15.9% with stimulants and no opioids; read as a share of stimulant-involved deaths it would be 8.6% of all deaths. The sentence allows both.
Abstract ('primarily methamphetamine'), Introduction ('mostly methamphetamine'), Data Sources 2nd paragraph ('primarily includes methamphetamine and other amphetamines'); no share given.

risk_of_bias.note: JBI prevalence fits a surveillance count. I agree with all nine items and with overall moderate. Item 6 (partial yes) could also cite that SUDORS involvement is a certifier's attribution of cause, not detection, which helps validity but adds certifier variation (item 7).

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 1. Sample frame appropriate to the target population
4. Study subjects and setting described in detail
5. Data analysis with sufficient coverage of the identified sample
risk_of_bias_domains.note: Main-text footnote ¶¶¶ adds that the circumstance subset's demographics are similar to the full sample's.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 6. Valid methods for identifying the condition
7. Condition measured in a standard, reliable way across participants

risk_of_bias_domains.note: The with/without-opioid contrasts are also crude, not age-standardized (see missed).

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 9. Adequate response rate, or low rate managed

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. The three overreaching statements are verified at Discussion 4th, 6th and 2nd/5th paragraphs. The quotation 'suggests increased drug potency or differential access' is verbatim. On point (3): the age argument is the decisive one. The hypertension remark is weaker, because the report does not say whether the cited figure of about 10% for US adults includes hypertension (its source, ref. 5, was not read).

missed: Footnote symbols are reused with different meanings in the main text, Figure 1 and the Table. Main-text §§ is the involvement rule, Table §§ the circumstance-data rule. Main-text ¶¶ is age adjustment, Table ¶¶ missing values. Main-text ††† is the jurisdiction rule, Table ††† history of stimulant use. Locators that put a bare symbol next to the Table (key finding 1; anchor 11 of cl_meth_us_trends) should say 'main-text footnote' or use the Table's own symbols (* for involvement, § for jurisdictions).

The with- and without-opioid contrasts are crude. Among methamphetamine-involved deaths, those without opioids were much older (64% vs 39% aged 45 or older), so part of the cardiovascular-history difference (39.3% vs 19.8%) may reflect age. The report does not age-standardize these within-SUDORS comparisons, only the comparison with US adults, which the card already flags.

Two small rounding slips in the Discussion. In the 4th paragraph, 43.1% of all deaths (stimulants with opioids) is called 'almost 45%'. In the 5th, 49,209 deaths (15.9%) are 'approximately 50,000 (15%)'. Minor; cite the Results figures.
